# plug

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/kit/plug"
```

Package plug is where kit's opt-in subsystems plug in: the HTTP engine, the frontends' file server and the process sampler of the runtime graph (framework/kit/server), the Studio's event stream and its profiler (framework/kit/studio), the stores and the databases (framework/kit/store), the queues (framework/kit/queue). kit reads what they registered through the hooks declared here, and imports none of the SDK packages behind them: a product that does not import a subsystem neither links nor initialises its packages.

It is also the contract between kit's core and the subsystems ADR 0179 takes out of it, as database/sql/driver is between database/sql and a driver: the store subsystem's engine over documents, its siblings, kit's scope on a database and its migrations ([Stores](#Stores)), which framework/kit/store sets; the refusals an engine says in kit's terms ([Refusal](#Refusal)); what kit's transactions offer an engine that takes part in them ([Transaction](#Transaction)); and the queue subsystem's brokers and their consumer ([Queues](#Queues)), which framework/kit/queue sets.

The package imports the standard library and the framework's model only, so that kit and every subsystem can import it.

## Variables

<a name="NewHTTPServer"></a>
```go
var NewHTTPServer atomic.Pointer[func(cfg HTTPConfig) HTTPServer]
```

NewHTTPServer builds the HTTP engine an app in the server profile serves on; nil until framework/kit/server is imported.

<a name="NewStaticFiles"></a>
```go
var NewStaticFiles atomic.Pointer[func(fsys fs.FS, csp string) (http.Handler, error)]
```

NewStaticFiles builds the file server of a frontend's tree; nil until framework/kit/server is imported.

<a name="OpenEventStream"></a>
```go
var OpenEventStream atomic.Pointer[func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (EventStream, error)]
```

OpenEventStream opens a Server-Sent Events stream on w; nil until framework/kit/studio is imported.

<a name="Queues"></a>
```go
var Queues atomic.Pointer[QueueDriverConfig]
```

Queues is the queue subsystem: the brokers kit's consumers' queues run on and the migration of a queue's table on a database; nil until framework/kit/queue is imported. A product that declares a topic, a subscription, a watch, a queued command or a mailer whose outbox is on a database without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="SampleProcess"></a>
```go
var SampleProcess atomic.Pointer[func() *model.Process]
```

SampleProcess samples the running process — its heap, goroutines, collections and CPU time — for the runtime graph a serving app answers; nil until framework/kit/server is imported, and the graph then carries no process (ADR 0172).

<a name="Stores"></a>
```go
var Stores atomic.Pointer[StoreDriverConfig]
```

Stores is the store subsystem: the engines kit's stores run on, kit's scope on a database and the migrations of kit's tables; nil until framework/kit/store is imported. A product that declares a store or a database without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="StudioProfiler"></a>
```go
var StudioProfiler atomic.Pointer[ProfilerConfig]
```

StudioProfiler is the Studio's profiler; nil until framework/kit/studio is imported.

<a name="Broker"></a>
## type [Broker](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/queue_interface.go>)

Broker is one queue as kit's core uses it: a publication, the consumer that delivers it, and its dead letters. It grows by the sibling below.

```go
type Broker interface {
	// Consume delivers the queue's messages to cfg's handler until ctx ends
	// or the queue's storage fails.
	Consume(ctx context.Context, cfg ConsumeConfig) error
	// DeadLetters are up to maxLetters of the queue's dead letters, oldest
	// first.
	DeadLetters(ctx context.Context, maxLetters int) ([]DeadLetterValue, error)
	// Publish puts payload in the queue: in the transaction ctx carries for
	// its database, when it lives on one.
	Publish(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) error
}
```

<a name="Clock"></a>
## type [Clock](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/queue_interface.go>)

Clock is the app's clock as a queue stamps and waits on it: kit's core hands the one its app runs on, a test's manual clock included.

```go
type Clock interface {
	// After is a channel that receives the clock's instant once d passed.
	After(d time.Duration) <-chan time.Time
	// NewTicker is a ticker that fires every d.
	NewTicker(d time.Duration) Ticker
	// NewTimer is a timer that fires once d passed.
	NewTimer(d time.Duration) Timer
	// Now is the clock's instant.
	Now() time.Time
	// Since is how long ago t was, on the clock.
	Since(t time.Time) time.Duration
	// Sleep waits until d passed.
	Sleep(d time.Duration)
}
```

<a name="ConsumeConfig"></a>
## type [ConsumeConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/queue.go>)

ConsumeConfig is how a queue's consumer runs: its handler, how long it waits idle, how many messages it handles at once and takes at a time.

```go
type ConsumeConfig struct {
	// Handler handles one delivery: nil acknowledges it, an error has it
	// retried or, through DoNotRetry, dead-lettered at once. Every handler
	// kit runs tolerates a redelivery.
	Handler      func(ctx context.Context, d DeliveryValue) error
	// PollInterval bounds an idle wait.
	PollInterval time.Duration
	// Parallelism is how many deliveries are handled at once.
	Parallelism  int
	// BatchSize is how many messages the consumer takes at a time.
	BatchSize    int
}
```

<a name="Database"></a>
## type [Database](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/store_interface.go>)

Database is kit's scope on one database (ADR 0179 §2): the transactions kit.Transact opens on it, their savepoints, and the functions held until their end. The core knows a database only through it; the store package implements it over the SDK's sql. It grows by the siblings below.

```go
type Database interface {
	// Defer holds fn until the transaction ctx carries for the database
	// commits, and reports true; outside one it holds nothing and reports
	// false.
	Defer(ctx context.Context, fn func()) bool
	// InTransaction reports whether ctx carries a transaction of this
	// database.
	InTransaction(ctx context.Context) bool
	// OnAbort holds fn until the work of the scope ctx carries for the
	// database is undone, and reports true; outside one it holds nothing
	// and reports false.
	OnAbort(ctx context.Context, fn func(ctx context.Context)) bool
	// Transact runs fn in a transaction of the database, or in a savepoint
	// of the one ctx carries for it: nil commits or releases, an error
	// rolls back.
	Transact(ctx context.Context, fn func(ctx context.Context) error) error
}
```

<a name="QueueConfig"></a>
## type [QueueConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/queue.go>)

QueueConfig is what kit asks of one queue: where it lies, its policy, the app's clock, and for a mailer's outbox the sealing of what it keeps.

```go
type QueueConfig struct {
	// Name names the queue's node in a refusal: the consumer's or the
	// mailer's node ID.
	Name       string
	// Dir is the directory a file queue lies in; with no Database and no
	// Dir, the queue is in memory.
	Dir        string
	// Database keeps the queue, nil when Dir or memory does: a scope the
	// store subsystem's Database opened, whose transaction a publication in
	// it joins.
	Database   Database
	// Table is the queue's table on Database.
	Table      string
	// Policy is how the queue leases, retries and bounds its messages.
	Policy     QueuePolicyValue
	// Clock is the app's clock, which the queue stamps and waits on.
	Clock      Clock
	// Seal, when set, seals every payload on its way in — a mail's, in a
	// mailer's outbox on a database —, and Unseal opens one on its way out;
	// MaxPayload bounds a payload before it is sealed.
	Seal       func(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) ([]byte, error)
	// Unseal is the payload a box holds, the box as it lies when it does
	// not open.
	Unseal     func(ctx context.Context, box []byte) []byte
	// MaxPayload bounds a payload Seal seals.
	MaxPayload int
	// Wrap, when a test sets it, stands in front of the queue the subsystem
	// opens: a func(queue.Broker) queue.Broker of the SDK's queue, which
	// kit's core does not name. Nil in every app a product builds.
	Wrap       any
}
```

<a name="QueueDriverConfig"></a>
## type [QueueDriverConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/queue.go>)

QueueDriverConfig is what framework/kit/queue plugs into kit: how a consumer's queue opens, the migration that makes its table on a database, and how a delivery's handler says that no retry can help.

```go
type QueueDriverConfig struct {
	// Open opens one queue, as cfg places it: on a database, in a
	// directory, or in memory.
	Open           func(cfg QueueConfig) (Broker, error)
	// TableMigration is the migration that makes the queue table on a
	// database of the dialect named, at version.
	TableMigration func(dialect string, table string, version uint64) (MigrationValue, error)
	// DoNotRetry is err as a delivery's handler returns it when no retry
	// can help: its queue dead-letters the message at once.
	DoNotRetry     func(err error) error
	// NotRetryable reports whether err, a delivery's handler's, says that no
	// retry can help: what DoNotRetry returned, the product's own included.
	NotRetryable   func(err error) bool
}
```

<a name="QueuePolicyValue"></a>
## type [QueuePolicyValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/queue.go>)

QueuePolicyValue is how a queue leases, retries and bounds its messages: the SDK's queue policy, in kit's terms.

```go
type QueuePolicyValue struct {
	// VisibilityTimeout is how long a delivery is leased.
	VisibilityTimeout time.Duration
	// RetryDelay is the wait after a message's first failure, doubled after
	// each, up to MaxRetryDelay.
	RetryDelay        time.Duration
	// MaxRetryDelay bounds the wait before a retry; zero leaves it unbound.
	MaxRetryDelay     time.Duration
	// MaxDeliveries is how often a message is delivered before it is
	// dead-lettered.
	MaxDeliveries     int
	// MaxMessageBytes bounds a message; zero is the queue's own bound.
	MaxMessageBytes   int
}
```

<a name="StoreConfig"></a>
## type [StoreConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/store.go>)

StoreConfig is what kit asks of one store's engine: the store, its key and its indexes over documents, where it rests and what it keeps, and how its writes take part in kit's transactions.

```go
type StoreConfig struct {
	// Name is the store's, as a log line and a rollback name it.
	Name        string
	// Key is a document's key: the product's key function on its type,
	// wrapped once at the declaration. It reads the document's Value, which
	// the engine decodes first unless KeyAtRest gives the key.
	Key         func(d DocumentValue) string
	// KeyAtRest, when set, gives the key of a record as it rests, without
	// decoding it; false when it cannot.
	KeyAtRest   func(raw json.RawMessage) (string, bool)
	// Decode is the entity a document's JSON holds, which the engine keeps
	// as the document's Value.
	Decode      func(raw json.RawMessage) (any, error)
	// Indexes are the store's secondary indexes.
	Indexes     []IndexSpec
	// Data is the data directory the store rests in — the SDK's writable
	// file system, which the engine asserts — and Path its snapshot there;
	// a nil Data and a nil Database keep the store in memory.
	Data        fs.FS
	// Path is the store's snapshot in Data.
	Path        string
	// Database keeps the store, nil when the data directory or memory does:
	// a scope the store subsystem's Database opened.
	Database    Database
	// Table is the store's table on Database.
	Table       string
	// IndexKey is the key a table's index keys are hashed under, nil for
	// none: an index key reaches the table as its keyed hash.
	IndexKey    func(index string, key string) []byte
	// Call is the context one call of the engine on Database runs with: on
	// the transaction ctx carries for it, else on the pool, within the
	// database's timeout; done ends it.
	Call        func(ctx context.Context, write bool) (call context.Context, done func(), err error)
	// Versions is how many former versions of each record the engine keeps,
	// none when zero; Clock stamps them.
	Versions    int
	// Clock is the app's clock, which stamps a version.
	Clock       func() time.Time
	// Held reports whether a record's versions are held, and no write may
	// prune them: asked with the write's context, on a database inside its
	// transaction.
	Held        func(ctx context.Context, key string) bool
	// Stamp is what a write under ctx says about the version it makes.
	Stamp       func(ctx context.Context) StampValue
	// Transaction is kit's transaction, which the engine's writes take part
	// in.
	Transaction Transaction
}
```

	Database       func(cfg DatabaseConfig) (Database, error)

<a name="StoreEngine"></a>
## type [StoreEngine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/store_interface.go>)

StoreEngine is what a store runs on, over documents (ADR 0179 §2): the non-generic engine under Store\[T]. Its refusals are kit's ([Refusal](#Refusal)): the engine translates the SDK's before they reach the core. Every call takes the caller's context, which carries the transaction the call joins. It grows by the sibling interfaces below, never by a method (the SDK's ADR 0039).

```go
type StoreEngine interface {
	// Close releases the engine.
	Close() error
	// Count says how many documents the store holds.
	Count(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
	// Delete removes the document under key.
	Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
	// Entries returns up to limit documents as they rest, in key order.
	Entries(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]json.RawMessage, error)
	// Filter returns the documents keep accepts, in key order.
	Filter(ctx context.Context, keep func(d DocumentValue) bool) ([]DocumentValue, error)
	// Find returns the documents an index files under key, in key order.
	Find(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) ([]DocumentValue, error)
	// Get returns the document under key.
	Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (DocumentValue, error)
	// List returns every document, in key order.
	List(ctx context.Context) ([]DocumentValue, error)
	// Lookup returns the document a unique index files under key.
	Lookup(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) (DocumentValue, error)
	// Update applies fn to the document under key and stores the result,
	// atomically with respect to every other write of the store.
	Update(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func(d *DocumentValue) error) (DocumentValue, error)
	// Watch registers the functions told the key of every document written
	// and deleted, once the write stands.
	Watch(onWrite func(key string), onDelete func(key string))
	// Write stores d as mode says. The document and its index keys are kept
	// together, or neither.
	Write(ctx context.Context, d DocumentValue, mode WriteMode) error
}
```

<a name="Transaction"></a>
## type [Transaction](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/plug/store_interface.go>)

Transaction is kit's transaction as a store's engine takes part in it (ADR 0139, ADR 0178): the core implements it, an engine calls it with its caller's context.

```go
type Transaction interface {
	// AtCommit holds fn until the transaction ctx carries commits, and
	// reports whether it did: false outside one, where the caller runs it
	// now.
	AtCommit(ctx context.Context, fn func()) bool
	// Local reports whether ctx runs in a transaction that holds the data's
	// writer turn: a write in the data directory or in memory then records
	// what it replaces.
	Local(ctx context.Context) bool
	// Retell keeps fn, which announces a write on a database again when the
	// transaction ctx carries rolls it back.
	Retell(ctx context.Context, fn func())
	// Undo keeps restore, which a rollback of the transaction ctx carries
	// runs; nothing outside one. store names the store in a log line.
	Undo(ctx context.Context, store string, restore func(ctx context.Context) error)
}
```
